model_policy.cheap: Fast low-cost model with strong instruction following for bounded prose tasks.
model_policy.balanced: Mid-tier model for synthesis, governance, curricula, and operational design.
model_policy.strong: Highest-capability model reserved for thesis-critical synthesis, adversarial review, and integration.
model_policy.code: Low-cost coding-capable model for deterministic scripts and repository checks.

tasks.title: Define the Practice voice and lexicon
tasks.objective: Create a precise language system that keeps every artifact recognizably Practice without sounding like generic AI marketing.
requirements: Define voice attributes with positive and negative examples.
Define canonical terms: Practitioner, Practice, Guide, Lab, Story, Note, Project, capability ladder.
Create banned or discouraged language and replacement guidance.
Include headline, description, and call-to-action patterns.
acceptance: Both files distinguish product language from marketing hype.
Examples cover beginner, technical, organizational, and community contexts.
No new tagline replaces the locked positioning.

tasks.title: Write the founding manifesto
tasks.objective: Produce the canonical public manifesto that explains why Practice exists and calls Practitioners to action.
requirements: Use the Founding Brief as source material without merely restating it.
Lead with the implementation gap, not model hype.
Explain openness, practice, evidence, contribution, and the human-agent community model.
End with a concrete invitation.
acceptance: Readable as a standalone public artifact.
No fabricated market statistics or external claims.
Between 900 and 1,800 words.

tasks.title: Finalize capability ladder and knowledge taxonomy
tasks.objective: Turn the founding concepts into a usable classification system for members, content, channels, and contributions.
requirements: Define outcomes, entry evidence, exit evidence, and anti-patterns for Learn, Use, Automate, Build, Transform.
Define the artifact taxonomy and when to choose each artifact type.
Explain cross-role and cross-capability tagging.
Include concrete classification examples.
acceptance: A contributor can classify a new artifact without guessing.
Capability levels describe skills rather than status.
Taxonomy resolves Note vs Practice vs Lab vs Story vs Project.

tasks.title: Define governance
tasks.objective: Create lightweight, credible governance for an initially founder-led open-source community that can broaden over time.
requirements: Define founder, maintainer, contributor, and Practitioner responsibilities.
Define decision categories and approval paths.
Define how governance evolves based on demonstrated contribution.
Include conflict-of-interest, removal, and succession mechanisms without bureaucracy.
acceptance: Founder authority is explicit at launch.
Contribution can earn responsibility through transparent criteria.
Irreversible and policy decisions remain human-owned.

tasks.title: Define contribution system
tasks.objective: Make contributing easier than creating a polished artifact from scratch while maintaining quality.
requirements: Define contribution paths from correction through maintained Project.
Describe issue, branch, review, evidence, attribution, and release flow.
Define recognition based on usefulness rather than volume.
Include a first-contribution path for non-engineers.
acceptance: A newcomer can select and complete a contribution path.
The process supports Buzz discussion and Git review without duplicating source of truth.
Acceptance and rejection criteria are explicit.

tasks.title: Define code of conduct and moderation model
tasks.objective: Create conduct and moderation rules optimized for high-signal practical collaboration and human accountability.
requirements: Define expected and unacceptable behavior.
Define reporting, triage, evidence preservation, appeal, and enforcement roles.
Separate low-signal quality issues from conduct violations.
Define what agents may flag and what humans must decide.
acceptance: No autonomous banning or silent content removal.
Rules are enforceable rather than aspirational.
Private reporting and conflict handling are addressed.

tasks.title: Finalize licensing and attribution policy
tasks.objective: Operationalize the dual-license model and make reuse, commercial use, attribution, and third-party contributions unambiguous.
requirements: Use Apache-2.0 for code and CC BY 4.0 for content unless a file says otherwise.
Define attribution format for reused and adapted Practice content.
Define contributor certification or sign-off approach without adding unnecessary CLA friction.
Define third-party source handling and generated-content review.
acceptance: Consistent with LICENSE-CODE, LICENSE-CONTENT.md, and LICENSES.md.
Commercial reuse is permitted with attribution.
No legal claims beyond what the licenses support.

tasks.title: Define community health and outcome metrics
tasks.objective: Measure whether Practice creates capability and reusable knowledge rather than vanity activity.
requirements: Define activation, contribution, artifact reuse, implementation, evidence, response quality, retention, and maintainer health metrics.
Distinguish leading and lagging indicators.
Define data that should not be collected.
Provide a minimal manual measurement method for launch.
acceptance: Metrics connect to the north star.
No invented benchmarks or targets.
The initial system can be operated without custom analytics software.

tasks.title: Polish contributor repository experience
tasks.objective: Make the public repository understandable and actionable from the first screen.
requirements: Create a concise contributor quickstart.
Add structured Lab and Project proposal issue forms.
Reference existing templates and contribution rules.
Avoid duplicating full policies.
acceptance: Issue forms collect enough information for triage.
Quickstart includes both Git-native and Buzz-first paths.
All relative links resolve.

tasks.title: Audit and finalize Buzz channel information architecture
tasks.objective: Validate the launch channel set against the capability ladder and keep the community deliberately small and outcome-oriented.
requirements: Review every baseline channel for purpose, overlap, and launch necessity.
Keep construction and maintainer work private.
Use stream channels only.
Document rules for creating, renaming, archiving, or splitting channels later.
acceptance: No public channel lacks a distinct outcome.
Channel count is justified and not expanded casually.
community.json remains valid and every referenced file exists.

tasks.title: Design end-to-end member onboarding
tasks.objective: Move a new member from invitation through first useful contribution without requiring prior AI expertise.
requirements: Account for Buzz being invite-only.
Define invitation, identity setup, orientation, capability self-assessment, first action, and follow-up.
Create a self-assessment that routes to Learn, Use, Automate, Build, or Transform.
Include agent-assisted and human-assisted paths.
acceptance: A new member has one clear first action.
Onboarding does not depend on unavailable automation.
No private key handling is delegated to agents.

tasks.title: Polish all Buzz channel canvases
tasks.objective: Turn every channel canvas into a concise operating guide that prevents ambiguity and empty-channel syndrome.
requirements: Preserve the purpose of each channel.
Add what belongs, what does not, and a first action where useful.
Keep private-channel instructions operational.
Cross-link only when a real path exists.
acceptance: Every canvas is publishable and non-empty.
No canvas repeats the entire manifesto.
Tone follows brand/VOICE.md.

tasks.title: Polish Buzz seed messages
tasks.objective: Create one high-signal seed message per launch channel that demonstrates expected behavior and prompts useful participation.
requirements: Preserve each unique idempotency marker.
Use concrete prompts rather than generic welcomes.
Do not imply members, results, or activity that do not exist.
Keep announcement volume low.
acceptance: Every seed contains exactly one practice-seed marker.
Prompts can produce a reusable artifact or clear next action.
No message exceeds 350 words.

tasks.title: Harden the Buzz bootstrapper
tasks.objective: Make Buzz setup idempotent, dry-run-first, inspectable, and safe against current platform limitations.
requirements: Use only the launch-safe CLI surface in the platform snapshot.
Create missing stream channels, set topic/purpose/canvas, and seed messages once.
Never delete or archive.
Redact secrets from errors and reports.
Handle common JSON response shapes and actionable failures.
acceptance: Dry run requires no Buzz installation or credentials.
Apply requires explicit --apply and environment variables.
Re-running apply does not duplicate seed messages when recent history contains the marker.
Runbook includes rollback-by-manual-review, not destructive automation.

tasks.title: Create Buzz access and security runbook
tasks.objective: Define identity, key, channel, agent, data, backup, and incident practices for hosted Buzz operation.
requirements: Document owner identity backup and recovery responsibilities.
Define per-agent identity and least-membership matrix.
Classify content safe for hosted Buzz.
Define offboarding and suspected-compromise steps.
Separate hosted MVP from self-host revisit triggers.
acceptance: Consistent with official support constraints.
No secret is ever requested in a channel.
Human actions are explicit.

tasks.title: Finalize Practice Steward agent profile
tasks.objective: Create a deployable, bounded profile for the member-routing and onboarding agent.
requirements: Define mission, inputs, output formats, tools, channel access, escalation, prohibited behavior, and evaluation cases.
Optimize for routing to useful action, not long answers.
Include prompt-injection and unknown-policy handling.
acceptance: Profile can be copied into a Buzz agent setup.
No owner privileges required.
At least five evaluation scenarios.

tasks.title: Finalize Practice Librarian agent profile
tasks.objective: Create a deployable profile for distilling valuable community work into candidate artifacts.
requirements: Define artifact classification rules and attribution requirements.
Require links back to source threads.
Draft only; never merge or publish without review.
Include privacy boundaries and disagreement preservation.
acceptance: At least five evaluation scenarios.
Output contract maps cleanly to Practice artifact templates.
No private-channel material may be published by default.

tasks.title: Finalize Guide Maintainer agent profile
tasks.objective: Create a deployable profile for guide coherence, staleness detection, and maintenance proposals.
requirements: Define change-detection, source verification, versioning recommendation, and review packet formats.
Require primary sources for changing technical claims.
Never merge its own work.
acceptance: At least five evaluation scenarios.
Staleness and deprecation are distinct.
Agent cannot silently change capability taxonomy.

tasks.title: Finalize Research Auditor agent profile
tasks.objective: Create a deployable profile for current-fact verification and citation integrity.
requirements: Define primary-source hierarchy, as-of dates, claim-source mapping, uncertainty, and contradiction handling.
Define a compact audit report.
Disallow invented citations and unsupported extrapolation.
acceptance: At least five evaluation scenarios.
Reports identify exact claims and dispositions.
The agent does not rewrite strategy.

tasks.title: Finalize Release Editor agent profile
tasks.objective: Create a deployable profile for turning merged work into announcements and weekly releases without hype.
requirements: Define required inputs, artifact links, status checks, output formats, and prohibited claims.
Require merged or released source material.
Preserve evidence quality and uncertainty.
acceptance: At least five evaluation scenarios.
No unmerged work can be announced as complete.
Every summary links to canonical artifacts.

tasks.title: Finalize the Open Practice schema
tasks.objective: Create the canonical schema and authoring rules for reusable Practices.
requirements: Define required and optional metadata.
Define maturity states from proposed through verified and deprecated.
Define evidence-quality levels.
Include a worked classification example.
Keep author burden proportional to maturity.
acceptance: Template and schema agree.
A validator could be built from the rules.
Failure modes and evaluation are required for mature Practices.

tasks.title: Finalize the Practice Guide schema
tasks.objective: Create the canonical structure and maintenance rules for opinionated Guides.
requirements: Define audience, outcomes, prerequisites, modules, Practices, capstone, evaluation, and versioning.
Explain when a collection becomes a Guide.
Define update and deprecation rules.
acceptance: Template and schema agree.
Guides reference Practices rather than duplicating them unnecessarily.
A Guide has a clear completion outcome.

tasks.title: Design the AI-Native Practitioner flagship guide
tasks.objective: Create the coherent end-to-end map for Practice's flagship Guide.
requirements: Cover foundations, effective use, context engineering, automation, agents, agentic engineering, organizational AI, and frontier work.
Define module outcomes, prerequisites, capstones, and evidence.
Provide multiple paths for nontechnical, technical, and organizational Practitioners without fragmenting the core.
Avoid a vendor-specific course outline.
acceptance: Every module advances a capability.
The guide is usable before all modules are complete.
Frontier material is clearly separated from established Practice.

tasks.title: Write the Foundations module
tasks.objective: Write a practical foundations module covering models, context, tools, limitations, structured output, privacy, security, and evaluation.
requirements: Use exercises and checkable outcomes.
Prefer enduring concepts over volatile product details.
Explain probabilistic behavior and verification without oversimplification.
Include a capstone.
acceptance: A beginner can complete it without coding.
No unsupported current product claims.
Exercises produce artifacts or evidence.

tasks.title: Write the Effective Use module
tasks.objective: Teach deliberate use across research, analysis, writing, planning, learning, and professional work.
requirements: Teach task framing, context, iteration, critique, and output verification.
Include role-neutral patterns and role examples.
Distinguish assistance from delegated execution.
Include a capstone based on a real workflow.
acceptance: Not a prompt collection.
Includes decision rules for when not to use AI.
Produces measurable before/after evidence.

tasks.title: Write the Context Engineering module
tasks.objective: Teach instruction, context architecture, skills, memory, retrieval, tool definitions, and progressive disclosure.
requirements: Explain context as a designed system rather than a long prompt.
Cover source hierarchy, freshness, conflicts, and boundaries.
Include a reusable context-pack exercise.
Address privacy and token/cost constraints conceptually.
acceptance: Connects to the first Context Pack Practice.
Includes failure diagnosis.
Avoids vendor-specific context-window claims.

tasks.title: Write the Automation and Agents module
tasks.objective: Move Practitioners from workflow decomposition through reliable tool-using agents.
requirements: Begin with deterministic automation and human approval.
Define agent loop, tools, state, permissions, error paths, observability, and evaluation.
Explain when an agent is unnecessary.
Include a bounded automation capstone.
acceptance: Reliability and rollback are first-class.
Autonomy is treated as a design variable, not a goal.
No framework is required.

tasks.title: Write the Agentic Engineering module
tasks.objective: Teach repository context, specifications, planning, implementation, tests, verification, parallel agents, and delivery controls.
requirements: Define task decomposition and file ownership.
Cover worktrees, acceptance criteria, independent review, and CI.
Explain handoffs and context recovery.
Use Practice's own swarm as a worked example without claiming results not yet measured.
acceptance: Useful to experienced engineers.
Includes anti-patterns for uncontrolled parallelism.
Connects to the Verification Gate Practice.

tasks.title: Write the Organizational AI module
tasks.objective: Teach workflow discovery, opportunity assessment, knowledge architecture, enablement, governance, measurement, and operating models.
requirements: Start from work and business outcomes.
Define an opportunity map without invented ROI.
Address role-specific enablement and change.
Include governance proportional to risk.
Include an organizational capstone.
acceptance: Not a generic digital-transformation essay.
Connects interventions to measurable operating changes.
Distinguishes adoption from capability.

tasks.title: Create Practice 001: Reusable Context Pack
tasks.objective: Create the first reusable Practice for packaging stable instructions, sources, constraints, examples, and verification into recurring AI work.
requirements: Use the canonical Practice schema.
Include a minimal and advanced implementation.
Include maintenance and freshness checks.
Include evaluation and failure modes.
acceptance: Immediately reusable by a nontechnical Practitioner.
No vendor dependency.
Evidence section honestly labels the initial maturity.

tasks.title: Create Practice 002: Workflow Redesign
tasks.objective: Create a method for decomposing a recurring workflow and selecting deterministic, AI-assisted, agentic, and human-owned steps.
requirements: Include inventory, classification, risk, data access, approval, rollback, and measurement.
Provide a worked hypothetical example labeled as such.
Define a smallest safe experiment.
acceptance: Produces a concrete workflow map.
Does not assume automation is always beneficial.
Includes evaluation before expanding autonomy.

tasks.title: Create Practice 003: Agent Verification Gate
tasks.objective: Create a reusable acceptance gate for agent-produced research, content, code, configuration, or operations work.
requirements: Define artifact-specific checks and universal checks.
Include evidence, tests, diff review, source validation, and rollback.
Define when human approval is mandatory.
Include a compact checklist and machine-readable example.
acceptance: Applicable beyond software.
Rejects unsupported completion claims.
Connects acceptance criteria to actual evidence.

tasks.title: Create the Lab system and first experiment
tasks.objective: Define reproducible Labs and design the first experiment around low-cost models completing bounded artifact tasks.
requirements: Define hypothesis, fixed conditions, task set, rubric, cost capture, result format, limitations, and reproduction.
Do not invent results; leave the results section ready for execution.
Compare task completion quality, not general model intelligence.
acceptance: Template and schema agree.
Experiment can be run by another Practitioner.
No model is endorsed before results exist.

tasks.title: Create the Story system and an explicitly hypothetical sample
tasks.objective: Define evidence-grounded Practice Stories and demonstrate the format without fabricating a real case study.
requirements: Define evidence-quality levels and anonymization rules.
Require before, intervention, after, result, lessons, and artifacts.
Mark the sample prominently as hypothetical.
acceptance: No invented customer or metric.
Template and schema agree.
A real contributor can replace the sample with evidence.

tasks.title: Create the launch narrative
tasks.objective: Translate the manifesto into a compelling written launch story and flagship video brief that demonstrates the Practice thesis.
requirements: Explain the implementation gap and why open practice matters.
Use Dakota's builder/practitioner perspective without inventing biography.
Design the video around showing work, not a talking-head announcement alone.
End with one clear invitation.
acceptance: Written story and video brief share a thesis without duplicating wording.
No market statistics are required.
The call to action points to Buzz and canonical open artifacts.

tasks.title: Create the first ten flagship content briefs
tasks.objective: Create ten production-ready content briefs that generate useful open-source artifacts and community participation.
requirements: Each brief states hook, Practitioner outcome, demonstration, artifact produced, community prompt, and repurposing.
Mix individual, engineering, founder, and organizational use cases.
Include Making Companies AI-Native, Workflow Clinic, Build With Me, Practice Tested, and community showcase formats.
acceptance: Every episode produces or improves a canonical artifact.
No episode depends on a fabricated participant or company.
Sequence builds the Practice thesis progressively.

tasks.title: Create the social launch kit
tasks.objective: Create channel-appropriate launch copy and profile language without reducing Practice to AI tips.
requirements: Include pinned profile descriptions, launch posts, short-form scripts, founder bio, and response templates.
Preserve the same claim set across channels.
Use placeholders for URLs and handles.
acceptance: No invented traction or urgency.
Calls to action are specific.
Copy follows the voice system.

tasks.title: Design the first Practice Session
tasks.objective: Create a repeatable live Workflow Clinic that produces a reusable Practice artifact.
requirements: Define participant intake, selection, preparation, facilitation, artifact capture, consent, follow-up, and publication review.
Include roles for host, Steward, Librarian, and Research Auditor.
Include contingency paths when the workflow is sensitive or unsuitable.
acceptance: Session produces a concrete draft artifact.
No private data is exposed by default.
Participants can decline publication.

tasks.title: Create the maintainer operating runbook
tasks.objective: Define the recurring human and agent work required to keep Practice useful, current, and safe.
requirements: Cover inbox triage, questions, artifact review, agent review, releases, moderation, stale content, backups, and owner gates.
Define responsibilities and escalation.
Prefer queues and checklists over meetings.
acceptance: A maintainer can operate Practice without founder-only tribal knowledge.
Agent assistance is bounded and reviewable.
Includes failure and recovery procedures.

tasks.title: Design the public invitation funnel
tasks.objective: Bridge public discovery into an invite-only Buzz community without creating a fragmented community stack.
requirements: Define social/Git discovery, request or invite link, qualification if any, onboarding, and follow-up.
Keep public artifacts accessible without membership.
Include abuse prevention and revoked-invite handling.
Use Buzz as the hub after entry.
acceptance: Does not require a custom application.
Open-source access is never gated behind membership.
Metrics connect to ops/METRICS.md.

tasks.title: Define the weekly operating cadence
tasks.objective: Create a sustainable founder-plus-agents cadence that compounds artifacts rather than producing constant channel activity.
requirements: Define intake, build, review, release, Session, and maintenance cycles.
Separate continuous queues from scheduled review.
Show which agent prepares each packet and which human approves.
acceptance: No ceremony without an output.
Cadence can operate with a small community.
Includes a low-activity fallback.

tasks.title: Create launch checklist and owner review packet
tasks.objective: Assemble a concrete release gate and a compact packet Dakota can review without rereading the entire repository.
requirements: List automated checks, manual Buzz steps, public repository checks, content checks, agent permission checks, and rollback.
Summarize locked decisions, remaining gates, known Buzz constraints, and deferred work.
Do not mark an unchecked item complete.
acceptance: Every required artifact is linked.
Owner decisions are limited to OWNER_GATES.md or newly evidenced blockers.
Checklist distinguishes dry run, private beta, and public launch.

tasks.title: Audit current platform and license facts
tasks.objective: Independently verify every current claim about Buzz and licensing that appears in launch-critical artifacts.
requirements: Map claim to primary source, as-of date, disposition, and required correction.
Check that excluded Buzz capabilities remain excluded.
Check license descriptions against canonical sources.
Do not edit source artifacts.
acceptance: Every audited claim has a disposition.
Contradictions are explicit.
Report separates blocking and non-blocking findings.

tasks.title: Run adversarial editorial and coherence review
tasks.objective: Find contradictions, repetition, generic AI language, audience confusion, and weak operational guidance across the core corpus.
requirements: Review as a skeptical expert and a capable beginner.
Identify exact files and passages.
Test consistency with the voice and locked decisions.
Recommend deletions before additions.
Do not edit source artifacts.
acceptance: Findings are ranked by severity.
Each recommendation is actionable.
No strategy is invented beyond the founding brief.

tasks.title: Run a complete onboarding dry run
tasks.objective: Simulate a new nontechnical member, a technical builder, and an internal AI lead entering the community and taking a first action.
requirements: Trace public discovery through invitation, Buzz setup, start-here, channel selection, asking, contribution, and follow-up.
Record ambiguity, dead ends, empty-state problems, and agent escalation failures.
Do not edit source artifacts.
acceptance: All three personas complete or fail at explicit steps.
Every defect includes severity and proposed owner file.
No imagined Buzz capability is used.

tasks.title: Run repository integrity and release validation review
tasks.objective: Independently check structure, links, schemas, licenses, task state, generated files, and release validation behavior.
requirements: Run normal and release validation.
Inspect all relative links and referenced files.
Check for TODOs, placeholders, secrets, duplicate seed markers, and stale task status.
Do not edit source artifacts.
acceptance: Include exact commands and outputs.
Separate script defects from content defects.
No passing claim without evidence.

tasks.title: Integrate review findings and prepare final release
tasks.objective: Apply blocking review findings across the repository, reconcile conflicts, run release validation, and create the final integration report.
requirements: May edit any project artifact except locked decisions unless an owner gate is opened.
Resolve blocking findings and disposition non-blocking findings.
Run `python3 scripts/validate.py --release`.
Update release/OWNER_REVIEW.md with final manual actions.
acceptance: Release validation passes or the report says BLOCKED with exact evidence.
All review findings have a disposition.
No owner-only action is falsely marked complete.
